title: Make the first producer report account for every criterion
summary: The goal is to cut producer send-backs for incomplete criteria reports. The audience is the user, who pays for the second run, and the verifier. I'll make the brief, prompt and report schema push the producer to emit one criteria_check entry per numbered criterion, and add a measured before/after send-back rate. The cause I found in the code is that criteria are matched by text and any paraphrase counts as missing; I did not measure it on the named jobs, because their records are absent from my copy.

defaults_applied.how: The goal is to find why the first report misses criteria, then fix that, not make the send-back lenient.
Criteria run tests that exercise the brief and the unmet-criteria check, plus a measured before/after rate.
The finding cites code locations; rates are marked measured or estimate with sample size.
Criterion requiring cargo test, clippy and fmt --check to pass.
Decision note written for an outside reader.
One focused change on the producer brief, prompt and schema.
The outcome is a lower first-report send-back rate, checked by measurement, not just edited prompt text.
Behavior checked by running the named cargo tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code reading (run.rs unmet_criteria, criterion_key): a criterion counts as reported only if an entry has status met and matches its text after stripping numbering, kind tag, case, spacing and trailing punctuation. A paraphrase, shortened or merged entry, or an entry marked unmet, therefore reads as missing and triggers the send-back.

Likely causes, from reading briefs.rs reading_sections, producer.md line 10 and outputs.rs CriterionCheckOutput: the brief shows criteria as numbered '[kind] text' lines; the prompt says 'no number or kind tag' and gives no reminder to copy the text; the schema does not require the entry count to equal the criterion count. Producers also report the criterion as paraphrase, or omit content criteria they treat as obvious.

Fix scope: change how criteria are shown (an explicit copy-verbatim list or checklist skeleton in the producer brief), tighten the producer prompt (one entry per criterion, in order, text copied verbatim, evidence for each even for criteria already done) and the schema field docs. Whether to also make matching tolerant (e.g. match by position or by number) is the producer's call, recorded in docs/decisions.md.

Measurement: the named jobs' records are absent from the reader's copy. The producer cannot see them either, so the before rate must come from a mechanism that reads records (an existing or added introspection/xtask command, or a test fixture of the six jobs' counts). The after rate is measured on the first jobs run after the change and reported as an estimate if the sample is small.
The send-back itself stays (one send-back, then flagged). The change targets why the first report misses criteria; it does not remove the check.

acceptance_criteria.text: A short written finding (in docs/decisions.md or the change's report) names the cause of the missed criteria, citing run.rs unmet_criteria/criterion_key, the producer brief's criteria rendering, producer.md and the CriterionCheckOutput schema. It says which of the three suspects (prompt, schema, display) contributed.

Run cargo test -p athena-context: a test shows the producer brief lists every accepted criterion in a form the producer can copy verbatim and tells it to report one criteria_check entry for each, in order, with evidence, including criteria already satisfied.

crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md and the criteria_check field docs in outputs.rs say that every criterion gets an entry with its text copied exactly, a status and evidence, and that a report missing any entry is sent back.

Run cargo test -p athena-core: a test shows a first report that has one met entry per criterion (with number and kind tag stripped) is not sent back, and that a report omitting one criterion still is sent back once.

The send-back rate before the change is stated for the six named jobs (kb23, c2h3, 7qht, 0qcy, c4w4, skh5) with the records read to get it, and the rate after is stated from jobs run after the change. Each number is marked measured or an estimate, with its sample size, and any record that could not be read is named.
Run cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check: all pass.
A note in docs/decisions.md records the design call and the alternatives considered (prompt only, schema only, tolerant matching), written for an outside reader.

out_of_scope: Removing the send-back check or raising the number of send-backs.
Changes to the verifier brief, the reader prompt, or verdict logic.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, or workflows.
departures: The measurement needs records that neither reader nor producer can see, so a clean before/after number is harder than for a typical change. That raises cost, lowers the pass probability, and raises the chance of user intervention.
